chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no obligation of Hajj nor Umra upon the slave until he is freed.
ai.seo_question: Is Hajj obligatory for a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies that the financial and physical burdens of Hajj and Umra are suspended for a slave, as they lack full autonomy over their time and wealth. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that religious obligations (taklif) are contingent upon the capacity to fulfill them, which is restricted for those in servitude until emancipation. It highlights the gradual nature of spiritual duties, ensuring that slaves are not burdened before they gain the freedom to perform the pilgrimage independently.
